s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity weakness with sensory changes and autonomic dysfunction
salient_findings: Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
key_facts: 61-year-old woman with type II diabetes
1-year history of progressive lower-extremity weakness
100-lb unintentional weight loss
Weakness began in proximal left leg and gradually involved right leg and both hands
Worsening numbness and tingling in feet
Wheelchair-dependent within 6 months
Denies pain, flank pain, hematuria, fevers, visual changes, speech or swallowing difficulty
Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
Atrophy of hands and thighs
Sensation to light touch reduced in feet
Slight impairment of vibration and proprioception
Reflexes 2+ in upper extremities and absent at knees and ankles
Plantar responses flexor
Bladder catheterization yielded 1.8 L of retained urine
CSF analysis showed protein 175 mg/dL, glucose 105 mg/dL, 1 WBC, 0 RBC
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrated chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy with superimposed chronic lumbosacral plexopathy

shortlist.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes with elevated CSF protein

shortlist.label: Diabetic amyotrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Type II diabetes and progressive lower-extremity weakness with weight loss

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral femoral nerve enlargement and chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy

shortlist.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes with atrophy of hands and thighs

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Unintentional weight loss and progressive neurological decline with negative autoimmune panel

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive lower-extremity weakness, numbness, and tingling, along with electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrating chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy, are consistent with CIDP. The elevated CSF protein level also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Diabetic amyotrophy
rejected.why: While the patient has type II diabetes, the presence of demyelinating polyneuropathy and elevated CSF protein level are more suggestive of CIDP than diabetic amyotrophy.

rejected.label: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the patient's widespread weakness and sensory deficits, which are not limited to the lumbosacral region.

rejected.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
rejected.why: This is a hereditary condition, and the patient's age of onset and rapid progression are not typical for CMT.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic neuropathy
rejected.why: The comprehensive paraneoplastic antibody panel was negative, making this diagnosis less likely.
